title: Presentable cartesian monoidal localization of the Joyal model
statement:
Use simplicial sets, universes, quasicategories and coherent functors of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the Joyal model structure and categorical equivalences $W$ of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure], and the cartesian pushout-product property of [lem-coef-joyal-cartesian-pushout-product]. Combinatorial means locally presentable with set-generated weak factorization systems, as in [lem-coef-combinatorial-localization-presentability]; tractable means combinatorial with a set of generating cofibrations whose sources are cofibrant. Left proper means that a pushout of a weak equivalence along a cofibration is a weak equivalence.

The Joyal model category is left proper, combinatorial and tractable, and its underlying category is cartesian closed. Every simplicial set is cofibrant. Its homotopy coherent localization $q:N(\mathsf{sSet})\to\mathsf{sSet}[W^{-1}]_\infty$ is saturated: a strict simplicial map $f$ belongs to $W$ if and only if $q(f)$ is an equivalence. With its monoidal localization, this localization is equivalent as a symmetric monoidal infinity category to the cartesian monoidal infinity category $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$ of small quasicategories of [lem-coef-cat-infinity-colimits-cartesian-closure]. In particular $q$ is a strong symmetric monoidal functor on all simplicial sets, including the terminal unit: there are coherent equivalences $q(K\times L)\simeq qK\times qL$ and $q(\Delta^0)\simeq\mathbf1$. These assertions hold in each universe and after enlarging the ambient universe.

proof.text: Theorem 2.2.5.1 of HTT constructs the Joyal model structure in each universe, with monomorphisms as cofibrations and categorical equivalences as weak equivalences; the quasicategory convention and internal functor objects are those of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. The simplicial sets form the presheaf category on the small simplex category, so [lem-coef-presheaf-local-presentability] gives local presentability. The existing Mathlib leaf [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells] supplies the relative boundary-cell presentation of every monomorphism. The Joyal generating-trivial-cofibration statement [lem-coef-joyal-generating-trivial-cofibrations] supplies a small set $J_{\mathrm J}$ generating the trivial-cofibration class. Hence both weak factorization systems are set-generated and the model is combinatorial. The initial map $\varnothing\hookrightarrow K$ is degreewise injective for every $K$, so every object is cofibrant; therefore the generating cofibrations have cofibrant sources and the model is tractable.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1 and proof, Corollary 2.2.5.4; Appendix A.2.6 for combinatoriality; online PDF, archival source WANTED

proof.text: The Joyal model is left proper. Every simplicial set is cofibrant by Step 1, so the all-cofibrant left-properness lemma [lem-coef-all-cofibrant-left-proper] applies to the model-category structure supplied by [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. It gives, for every cofibration $i:A\to B$ and categorical equivalence $w:A\to A'$, that $B\to B\amalg_AA'$ is again a categorical equivalence. This is exactly left properness and does not use any Kan simplicial enrichment.

source.place: Corollary 2.2.5.4 and proof of Theorem 2.2.5.1; online PDF, archival source WANTED

proof.text: Degreewise products make simplicial sets cartesian closed, with terminal object $\Delta^0$. The cartesian pushout-product axiom is exactly [lem-coef-joyal-cartesian-pushout-product], while [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] gives the cofibrations, weak equivalences and all-object cofibrancy. Step 1 supplies local presentability and set-generated factorizations, so the hypotheses of [lem-coef-combinatorial-localization-presentability] apply: its coherent localization is presentable and receives a symmetric monoidal structure for which $q(K)\otimes q(L)\simeq q(K\times L)$ and whose unit is $q(\Delta^0)$. The construction is coherent and preserves small colimits separately in each variable.

source.place: Higher Algebra §1.3.4 (model localization), Proposition 4.1.7.4 and Example 4.1.7.6; online, archival source WANTED

proof.text: A homotopy coherent localization $q:N(\mathsf{sSet})\to\mathsf{sSet}[W^{-1}]_\infty$ at $W$ exists by [lem-coef-hammock-infinity-localization]: the homotopy coherent nerve of a locally Kan replacement of the hammock localization of $(\mathsf{sSet},W)$, with its full functor-infinity-category universal property; it is a quasicategory. By the Joyal-specific comparison [lem-coef-joyal-localization-cat-infinity] there is an equivalence $\Phi:\mathsf{sSet}[W^{-1}]_\infty\simeq\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$, induced by the Joyal--Bergner coherent-nerve Quillen equivalence, with $\Phi(qQ)\simeq Q$ naturally for every small quasicategory $Q$. This comparison concerns the ordinary Joyal model and imposes no Kan-enrichment hypothesis on its cartesian mapping objects, and it is compatible with enlarging the universe. Here $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$ is the cartesian closed infinity category of small quasicategories and coherent functors of [lem-coef-cat-infinity-colimits-cartesian-closure].

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1, Corollary 2.2.5.4 and Proposition 2.2.5.8; Higher Algebra §1.3.4; online, archival source WANTED

proof.text: The localization is saturated for arbitrary simplicial maps $f:A\to B$, with no Kan, fibrancy or quasicategory hypothesis on $A$ or $B$. The Joyal structure of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] is a model category in the sense of [lem-coef-model-localization-detects-weak-equivalences]: $\mathsf{sSet}$ is a presheaf category, hence complete and cocomplete, $W$ is retract closed with two-out-of-three, and both weak factorization systems are functorial. Since the target of $q$ is a quasicategory with the coherent localization universal property, [lem-coef-localization-homotopy-category] says that $q(f)$ is an equivalence if and only if its class is an isomorphism in $h(\mathsf{sSet}[W^{-1}]_\infty)$, and that $hq:\mathsf{sSet}\to h(\mathsf{sSet}[W^{-1}]_\infty)$ is an ordinary localization at $W$. By [lem-coef-model-localization-detects-weak-equivalences] applied to this ordinary localization, $hq(f)$ is an isomorphism if and only if $f\in W$. Hence $q(f)$ is an equivalence exactly when $f\in W$. By [lem-coef-joyal-functor-equivalence-test], membership in $W$ is equivalently the coherent functor-equivalence test $\operatorname{Fun}(B,C)\to\operatorname{Fun}(A,C)$ against every quasicategory $C$.

source.place: Corollary 2.2.5.4 and Proposition 2.2.5.8; online, archival source WANTED

proof.text: Products preserve $W$. For a simplicial set $X$, the functor $X\times-$ has the right adjoint $\operatorname{Fun}(X,-)$ of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Applying [lem-coef-joyal-cartesian-pushout-product] to $\varnothing\hookrightarrow X$ and a monomorphism $b$, the pushout-product is $X\times b$, so $X\times-$ preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations. By [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] it preserves weak equivalences between cofibrant objects, which are all objects by Step 1; by symmetry so does $-\times X$. Products are carried to products. For small simplicial sets $K,L$ factor $K\to RK$ and $L\to RL$ as trivial cofibrations followed by fibrations to $\Delta^0$ ([lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]); $RK,RL$ are quasicategories, and $K\times L\to RK\times L\to RK\times RL$ lies in $W$ by the previous paragraph. By Step 4, $\Phi q$ sends $RK,RL,RK\times RL$ and the two projections to the quasicategories $RK,RL,RK\times RL$ and their projections. By [lem-coef-cat-infinity-colimits-cartesian-closure] the degreewise product of two quasicategories, with its projections, is their product in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$ (it is the variable of the exponential adjunction $\operatorname{Fun}(T,\operatorname{Fun}(A,E))\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(T\times A,E)$), and $\Delta^0$, the empty product, is terminal. Hence $q$ sends each product square $K\leftarrow K\times L\to L$ to a product diagram and $\Delta^0$ to a terminal object. Monoidal comparison. Since $W$ contains the isomorphisms, is closed under composition and is preserved by $X\times-$ and $-\times X$, [lem-coef-relative-symmetric-monoidal-localization] applies to the cartesian symmetric monoidal nerve of $(\mathsf{sSet},\times,\Delta^0)$: it gives the localized symmetric monoidal structure with strong symmetric monoidal $q^\otimes$, $q(K)\otimes q(L)\simeq q(K\times L)$ and unit $q(\Delta^0)$, coherently. Its canonical maps $qK\otimes qL\to qK\otimes\mathbf 1\simeq qK$ are $q$ of the projections $K\times L\to K\times\Delta^0=K$, so by the previous paragraph this structure is cartesian, with terminal unit; this is the structure of Step 3, which is computed by the same products since every object is cofibrant. The structure on $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$ is cartesian by [lem-coef-cat-infinity-colimits-cartesian-closure]. The cartesian-monoidal uniqueness principle [lem-coef-cartesian-monoidal-structure-uniqueness] therefore upgrades $\Phi$ to a strong symmetric monoidal equivalence, unique up to a contractible space of choices, with the coherent-nerve comparison [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] supplying $\Phi$ on underlying categories.

source.place: Higher Algebra Proposition 4.1.7.4 and Example 4.1.7.6; HTT Proposition 2.2.5.8; online, archival source WANTED

proof.text: The strong monoidal structure gives coherent equivalences $q(K\times L)\simeq qK\times qL$ and $q(\Delta^0)\simeq\mathbf 1$. Every construction above is performed in a chosen universe of small simplicial sets. Enlarging the ambient universe (Step 4 and [lem-coef-joyal-localization-cat-infinity] are compatible with it) only enlarges the test quasicategories and coherent functor categories; the universe clauses in [lem-coef-cat-infinity-colimits-cartesian-closure] and the Joyal model statement show that the same comparison and saturation argument remains valid.
